chain.note: The two trees are the same route (S1 bank-exchange network -> frames -> labels -> s<Wm -> eta and tau=1-2^{-50} -> interchange recurrence; S2 phase network -> layer recurrence; S3-S6 transforms, resampling, recovery and cost), and neither breaks. The one difference is at the source of the central saving: Plan B derives L<N/2 from the exact ratios 100/539 and 101/539 (S1.5.6, lines 1105-1110) before s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m, whereas Plan A only asserts L<N/2 in S1.5's claim. A's chain still reaches s<Wm through the stated deficits (S1.5.7, S1.5.9) and the exact eta values (S1.5.10), so the difference is slight.

errors.says: Writing a row number as r=Wg+w and sending the whole row to stream w gives W streams of equal shape, each of volume V/W (stated unconditionally).
errors.paper: Equal shape and volume V/W hold only when W divides R: 'If W divides R, each stream has address set [P]x[R/W]x[B] ... Thus the streams have the same shape and each has volume V/W.'

overall.reason: A full diff shows the plans are identical except for Plan B's step S1.5.6. That step states the exact loss ratios L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2 (lines 1105-1110). This is checklist sub-step L5, and it is the paper's ground for L<N/2, the inequality behind the strict saving s<Wm; Plan A only asserts L<N/2. No error separates the plans (the one minor issue, the dropped W | R condition in S1.1.4, is in both), so B is preferred by a single constant-level sub-step.
